newsitem.title: USA: CME HOGS END WEAKER ON TECHNICAL FUND SELLING.
newsitem.headline: CME HOGS END WEAKER ON TECHNICAL FUND SELLING.

text.p: CME hog futures retreated late to close mostly weaker as chart-based fund selling and sell stops were triggered, traders said.
Pork bellies finished lower after an early spurt that took August up the 3.000 cent per lb limit.
Hog futures ended 0.675 cent a lb lower to 0.200 higher with October off most at 71.850 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.400 to 0.250 cent lower. August fell 1.400 to 81.125 cents.
October broke through technical support at 72.100 cents and sank to fill the gap left in charts after the June Hogs and Pigs report. Late long liquidation kept prices pressured, they said.

August ended down despite expectations of steady cash hogs Tuesday. Hog runs were a fairly light but were seen rising this week. More hogs will be available for slaughter this week and cash hog prices will likely be depressed after any strength on Tuesday. Also, August is at a premium to the latest CME lean hog index, they added.
The latest CME lean hog index was off $0.60 to $79.99 per cwt. The quote compared with the August close at 80.400 cents.
Refco and Cargill Investor Services sold while Lind-Waldock bought, traders said.
In hog options, Iowa Grain actually sold October 74 calls and bought August 80 puts, pit sources said.

A buy stop placed just above early lows in August CME pork belly futures was touched off and that month shot up for a limit gain of 3.000 cents per lb before tumbling again for closing losses. The buy stop was placed when futures were trading lower and the rally came as a surprise, especially with cash belly prices falling further Monday, traders said.
USDA's carlot pork report near midday Monday indicated pork bellies sold $3.00 per cwt lower in thin activity. The drop follows a sharp slide in cash belly prices last week.
Locals actively sold August pork belly futures at the upper limit and mixed pressure continued late.
Next year belly contracts followed the lead of August, they added.
Prudential Securities was the buyer in August. Refco bought February early before R.J. O'Brien and E.D.&F. Man sold, pit sources said.
